messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: n_eff & rhat from extracted samples?
parts: If I have a matrix of samples from rstan::extract(stanfit_obj,pars='mu'), how would I go about computing the n_eff & rhat values that would otherwise appear in the summary table printed from print(stanfit_obj)?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: n_eff & rhat from extracted samples?
parts:
Oh, found it by delving into the source. First, you need to do the extract as:

    mu = rstan::extract(post,pars='mu',permuted=F)

so that the chains are distinguished (not mixed & shuffled as occurs when permuted=T, the default for rstan::extract). 

Then you can do:

    rstan:::ess_rfun(mu)

for n_eff, and:

    rstan:::split_rhat_rfun(mu)

for rhat. If mu is a vector parameter, then you need to do 

    rstan:::ess_rfun(mu[,,1])

for the 1st element of the vector, etc.

On Sun, Oct 23, 2016 at 2:16 PM, Mike Lawrence <mike....@gmail.com> wrote:
If I have a matrix of samples from rstan::extract(stanfit_obj,pars='mu'), how would I go about computing the n_eff & rhat values that would otherwise appear in the summary table printed from print(stanfit_obj)?

messages.subject: Re: n_eff & rhat from extracted samples?
parts:
On Sunday, October 23, 2016 at 1:58:51 PM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:
Oh, found it by delving into the source. First, you need to do the extract as:

    mu = rstan::extract(post,pars='mu',permuted=F)

so that the chains are distinguished (not mixed & shuffled as occurs when permuted=T, the default for rstan::extract). 

Then you can do:

monitor(mu)

possibly passing a value for `warmup` depending on what you did for `inc_warmup` in `extract`.

Ben
